claims.text: Rescuers in western Colombia searched under rubble following what has been called the country's strongest earthquake this century.
A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia at 07:34 local time (12:34 GMT) on Monday.
Official figures confirm more than 180 people died in the earthquake, while aggregated figures from local officials indicate the death toll may exceed 240.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella reported that almost 2,600 people were injured, nearly 200 remain missing, over 1,100 homes were destroyed, and over 8,000 homes were damaged.
In Cali, Mayor Alejandro Eder reported 95 deaths, 239 people trapped, 949 injured, and 45 buildings partially or fully collapsed.
In the Calima neighbourhood of Cali, four children died and 30 were referred to care centres after a section of the Gimnasio Calima school collapsed.
Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder ordered a curfew starting at 20:00 local time on Tuesday until 06:00 on Wednesday to prevent looting.
Colombia's geological service reported that more than 70 aftershocks occurred following Monday's earthquake, including two 3.6-magnitude quakes early on Tuesday.
In Pereira, 79 people were confirmed dead by the city's fire department, and local authorities implemented a car-free day to facilitate search efforts.
Manizales Mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas stated that five people were killed and 60 buildings partially or totally collapsed in the city.
Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares reported that 164 Spanish citizens were missing in Colombia following the earthquake.
Local authorities in western Colombia reported that more than 3,000 people remain missing and nearly 5,000 homes were damaged.
Airports in Quibdo, Pereira, Manizales, Armenia, Cartago, and Buenaventura were closed due to earthquake damage.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of disaster and announced temporary rental subsidies for affected families.
The European Union activated its Copernicus satellite service to assist Colombian authorities in damage assessment and rescue operations.
The Colombian Association of Capital Cities reported that at least 132 people were killed and more than 570 were injured as of Monday afternoon.
On June 24, twin earthquakes struck the northern coast of Venezuela, killing more than 6,000 people.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella took office on the Friday preceding the earthquake.
Syrians gathered outside the Justice Palace in Damascus after a court sentenced ousted President Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia and former security official Atef Najib to death.
Bashar al-Assad fled Damascus for Moscow with his family after his regime was overthrown in December 2024.
Atef Najib, former head of political security in Daraa province, was sentenced to death in person while standing in a cage wearing a prison uniform.
The detention and alleged torture of a group of teenagers accused of writing anti-government graffiti in Daraa in March 2011 ignited nationwide protests that escalated into civil war.
The Damascus court sentenced six former military and security officials to death in absentia, including Bashar al-Assad's brother Maher al-Assad and former defense minister Fahd al-Freij.
Ahmed al-Sharaa became president of Syria following an 11-day campaign that ended the Assad family's rule in December 2024.
Atef Najib was detained by Syrian security forces in early 2025.
Judge Fakhareddine al-Aryan announced the death sentence against Atef Najib during a court session broadcast live on state television.
A Syrian court sentenced Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher al-Assad to death in absentia for crimes committed during Syria's 14-year civil war, which claimed approximately 500,000 lives.
About 1,500 mostly Alawite civilians were killed in retaliatory violence in March 2025, and over 1,700 people were killed in Suweida province in July 2025.
Bashar al-Assad became the designated heir to the presidency after his older brother, Basil, died in a car accident in 1994.
Atef Najib was sanctioned by the U.S. Department of the Treasury in April 2011.
Russia released former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman from prison after more than four years following talks between U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed that Russia released Robert Gilman on a humanitarian basis without demanding a prisoner exchange.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the administration is seeking the return of Stephen Hubbard, who was sentenced in Russia in October 2024 to nearly seven years in prison.
Robert Gilman, 32, was scheduled to land at Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday night.
Global Reach chief strategy officer Eric Lebson stated that Gilman was transferred in June from a prison hospital to a psychiatric ward in a dissociative stupor due to prison abuse.
U.S. Senator Ed Markey stated that Gilman suffered from severe pneumonia and entered a near-death, catatonic state prior to his release.
Robert Gilman served in the U.S. Marine Corps from August 2019 until August 2020.
U.S. officials stated that Gilman would be flown to a rehabilitation centre in San Antonio, Texas, for medical treatment following his return.
Robert Gilman's father, Vladimir Gilman, stated in an October 2024 op-ed that the police officer involved in the 2022 incident dropped charges and sustained no injuries.

Gilman was arrested in January 2022 on a train to Moscow for allegedly kicking a police officer while drunk, receiving an initial sentence of three and a half years that was extended to 10 years following alleged assaults on prison staff.
Advocate Eric Lebson stated that five other Americans remain in Russian detention: Aleksandr Antonov, David Barnes, Olga Jezler, Andre Khachatoorian, and Chuck Zimmerman.
Hungary's parliament elected former Supreme Court chief András Baka as head of state by a vote of 140 to 6.
All 51 attending lawmakers from Viktor Orbán's Fidesz party walked out of the parliamentary chamber in protest before the vote.
The government led by Prime Minister Péter Magyar abolished the Sovereignty Protection Office and established the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office.
Constitutional amendments introduced by the Tisza party limited the prime minister to two terms in office and members of parliament to three terms.
Public service radio and TV in Hungary have been off the air since July 9 while news programming undergoes restructuring.
András Baka served as a judge at the European Court of Human Rights for nearly 20 years before becoming president of Hungary's Supreme Court in 2009.
In December 2011, Viktor Orbán's government removed András Baka as Supreme Court president three years before his term expired.
Prime Minister Péter Magyar initially offered the presidency to chess star Judit Polgár, who declined the role.
András Baka is scheduled to assume the presidency of Hungary on August 19.
Following his 2011 removal from the Supreme Court, András Baka won an unfair dismissal case against Hungary at the European Court of Human Rights.
A U.S. Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles into the engine room of the Panama-flagged M/V Vela Nova in the Gulf of Oman to disable its steering gear.
U.S. Central Command stated that as of August 11, it had redirected 55 commercial vessels attempting to run the Iranian blockade, disabled three non-compliant vessels, and boarded two.
Yemen's government reported that Houthi strikes on a cargo ship carrying Saudi military equipment in the Red Sea killed six people and injured 10.
A June memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran contained a preliminary plan for a $300 billion reconstruction fund.

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated that the Strait of Hormuz "will not be opened until the United States changes its behaviour and accepts Iran’s conditions."
Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran on Tuesday for mediation talks with Iranian officials.
The M/V Vela Nova is the third ship forcibly halted by U.S. forces since Washington reinstated its ports blockade on July 14.
During an earlier blockade between April 13 and June 18, U.S. forces disabled nine vessels and redirected more than 140 ships attempting to reach Iranian ports.
The U.S. Navy has deployed more than 15 warships in the Arabian Sea, including two aircraft carriers and an amphibious assault ship.
During the altitude loss on the Air India flight, a stall warning flashed and the first officer executed a stall-recovery response.
Air India flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi dropped around 300 feet during cruise on August 4, injuring 20 passengers and four crew members.
The confirmatory drug test for the pilot-in-command of the August 4 Air India flight returned positive for a banned substance.
Air India's outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson met with Civil Aviation Ministry and DGCA officials on Tuesday evening following the test results.
Former Ethiopian Airlines chief executive Tewolde Gebremariam was appointed as Air India's new CEO and managing director.
An official confirmed that the pilot-in-command tested positive for marijuana in the confirmatory drug test.
The preliminary defect report noted that the autopilot disconnected and triggered a stall warning and flight control ECAM message prior to the loss of altitude.
France's Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety (BEA) and Airbus technical representatives are assisting India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau.
Seventeen people were hospitalised following the sudden 300-foot drop on Air India flight AI2379.

DGCA regulations dictate that a pilot testing positive for psychoactive substances for the first time must undergo de-addiction, while a second positive result leads to a three-year licence suspension and a third leads to permanent cancellation.

External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that India is examining the national security and regional stability implications of the defence agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Mecca on August 7.
A central provision of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement states that an armed attack against any one of the three signatories will be regarded as an attack against all three.
The trilateral pact builds on a mutual defence agreement concluded by Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in September.
External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called on the international community to hold Pakistan accountable after protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir caused over 90 deaths.
